# pmon_policies (Data Source)

Every Cedar policy, shipped and authored alike.

Cedar evaluates all of them on every decision and a `forbid` always beats a `permit`, so reading the whole set is the only way to reason about what a new policy will actually do. Filter on `origin` to separate the shipped `SYSTEM` presets from your own.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pmon_policies" "all" {}

# A disabled policy is inert but still listed, which is easy to miss when reading the console.
output "disabled_policies" {
  value = [for p in data.pmon_policies.all.policies : p.name if !p.enabled]
}

# Shipped presets cannot be managed as resources; these are the ones you authored.
output "authored_policies" {
  value = [for p in data.pmon_policies.all.policies : p.name if p.origin == "USER"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `policies` (Attributes List) The policies, as pmon reports them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies))

<a id="nestedatt--policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies`

Read-Only:

- `cedar_src` (String) The Cedar source.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy takes part in decisions. A disabled policy is inert but still listed.
- `id` (Number) pmon's internal id. Shipped policies have negative ids.
- `name` (String) Policy name.
- `origin` (String) `SYSTEM` for a shipped policy, which is immutable, or `USER`.
- `system_key` (String) Stable key identifying a shipped policy across upgrades. Null for authored policies.
- `updated_at` (String) When the policy was last written.
- `updated_by` (String) Principal that last wrote the policy.
